subject: NULL being printed during reactive transition of inputs - possible to skip output?

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: NULL being printed during reactive transition of inputs - possible to skip output?
parts:
runGist("https://gist.github.com/tcash21/6236078")

When this applications starts, you'll notice two errors, since both of my inputs are initially NULL. 

Listening on port 8100
Error in if (input$input1 == input$input2) return() : 
  argument is of length zero
Error in if (input$input1 == input$input2) return() : 
  argument is of length zero

I don't ever want input1 == input2, so I added a check in output$show:
if(input$input1 == input$input2)
        return()

However, when I set input1 to "B", you can see NULL flash on the screen. The end result does ultimately occur (if I set input1 = "B" while input2 = "B", input2 should reset to all values that are NOT "B"). I would think a NULL would never be printed since I'm checking for that case in output$show and returning if it's true. Should I be placing the logic elsewhere? Reactivity is really throwing my brain into a blender.

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: NULL being printed during reactive transition of inputs - possible to skip output?
parts:
Oh, it might be because renderPrint, which tries to display the returned value as it would be if it were returned at the R console. That is, if the object has a visible flag, it would call print() on it; if not, it won't.

You can avoid this by using return(invisible()) instead of just return().

To illustrate, this is what happens at the R console:

f <- function() { return() }
f()
# NULL

g <- function() { return(invisible()) }
g()
# <no output> 

If you want to know more about the visible flag, see ?withVisible.

-Winston
